T1Q1: Right magnitude (~62% cheaper) but quotes EECA's $480-vs-$180 compare-options scenario instead of the $284/yr product-page figure. Both are in the KB, which flags the discrepancy itself. No date cited.
T1Q2: Leads with the electric-cylinder comparison, not the gas/LPG one asked about. Neither the 60% (gas) nor 75% (LPG) figure appears.
T1Q3: $7,000 correct. Lifespan given as '10-12 years, according to EECA's data' - invented and misattributed; EECA's basis is 15 years.
T1Q4: Programme and 50-90% range broadly right. Omits the $3,450 cap and the $400-700 household contribution; overstates insulation grant as 'up to 90%' generally.
T1Q5: Eligibility criteria fabricated ('low income', 'not receiving heating or cooling grants', 'health requirements'). Misses pre-2008 build, CSC/SuperGold, area eligibility. Also reads a full URL aloud, which the system prompt forbids.
T1Q6: Answers with boil speed (20-40%) rather than efficiency. Directionally correct but omits gas ~30% vs induction 80-90% and 'half the energy'.
T1Q7: $2,980 and $17/yr both correct. Omits the gas connection charge (>$580/yr) - the larger saving and the point of the question.
T1Q8: Cooler surface, no open flame, reduced burn risk all correct. Omits combustion by-products.
T1Q9: Invents '55-65%' attributed to Rewiring. The KB holds EECA's 7,000kg and 2,000kg over 15 years; neither used.
T1Q10: Uses Rewiring advocacy figures ($1,000/yr, 3x, $183/yr) in place of EECA's $122 (gas) and $352 (LPG). The $122 figure is in the KB.
T1Q11: Heat pump correctly identified as lowest-cost, lowest-emissions. Omits the wood/pellet and gas/LPG ranking.
T1Q12: Says insulation must be met 'by the start of 2029' and landlords are 'not specifically required to install insulation'. Compulsory since 1 July 2019. Understates a legal obligation.
T1Q13: Invents 'a heater at least 90% efficient'. The standard is a fixed heater for the main living room meeting a minimum capacity.
T1Q14: Conflates rooftop install share with generation share; gives 3.7% of connections and 'potentially 70%'. Expected ~1% of consumption (2021), up to ~6% by 2035.
T2Q1: 22% production drop approximated as 20%. Asserts 'increasing need for gas imports' - NZ does not import natural gas. Omits the 27% reserves fall / 1,300 to 948 PJ.
T2Q2: Invents a 'Maui-Tonga Tui (MTT)' field. Omits Mangahewa, Kupe, 109 TJ/day, and the 100 PJ-by-2026 forecast.
T2Q3: Wholly fabricated and geographically inverted: 'Whittaker Field, South Island, near Mount Cook', piped to the North Island. NZ gas is Taranaki; the South Island has no reticulated network. Highest-harm answer in the run.
T2Q4: Cost ordering right. Omits that LPG is bottled/trucked and available nationwide while piped gas is North Island only - the practical distinction.
T2Q5: 'No blanket ban' is correct, and Rewiring's position is explicitly attributed as advocacy. Attributed to the Electricity Authority (wrong body); omits the 2021 Commission recommendation.
T2Q6: Invents a 2035 phase-out and a '75% by 2030' target attributed to the Electricity Authority. The Gas Transition Plan is MBIE-led with no such targets.
T2Q7: $550-750/yr overstates the $365-580 range that is in the KB verbatim ($1-1.60/day). Misattributed to the Electricity Authority.
T2Q8: Gives '$4,000 over 15 years' and says no cooktop saving is available. Misses the daily gas connection charge, which is the answer.
T2Q9: Price pressure and shortage risk are right, but attributed to Rewiring when MBIE chunks were retrieved and MBIE is the authoritative source. Omits the advice to plan for alternatives.
T2Q10: Correct that constrained gas contributed. Attributed to Rewiring; omits $800/MWh, low hydro and wind.
T3Q1: Dates wrong (2020-2022 vs 1 Jul 2021 - 31 Dec 2023). Omits the fee side of the scheme entirely.
T3Q2: Wrong end date and a fabricated cause ('changes in the ETS that removed the discount from electricity costs'). Correctly notes no current subsidy.
T3Q3: States EVs are exempt from RUC, attributed to EECA and the Commerce Commission. EVs have paid RUC since 1 April 2024. Directly costs a visitor money.
T3Q4: Answers with a petrol-equivalent c/L figure instead of the RUC rate. $76/1,000km absent.
T3Q5: Invents a charge 'levied on the sale of alternative fuelled vehicles'. Misses electronic RUC and the petrol excise phase-out.
T3Q6: Invents '430 public EV chargers' attributed to the Electricity Authority, plus operators 'ChargePoint and Veloce'.
T3Q7: Invents a 150,000-charge-point 2030 target (actual: 10,000) with garbled double attribution.
T3Q9: EVRoam described as a European roaming card. It is NZTA's national charger database.
T3Q10: Asserts NZTA is 'not typically involved' in public EV charging. NZTA publishes the national guidance the question asks about.
T3Q11: Correct that EVs are cheaper to run, but the supporting figures are fabricated and the petrol comparison uses nonsensical units ($/kWh for a petrol car). No RUC offset.
T3Q12: Core claim correct. '90% less CO2' is invented precision; renewable-grid reasoning is present.
T3Q13: Concludes EV uptake 'may not necessarily increase overall electricity demand' - the opposite of MBIE's forecast, which is in the KB.
T3Q14: Invents a 'Zero Emissions Discount' successor scheme.
T3Q15: Invents RUC calculated on ETS-excess emissions.
T4Q1: 85.5% for 2024 correct and dated. Attributed to the Electricity Authority rather than MBIE; omits the 96.4% quarter.
T4Q2: Wrong year and wrong mix (hydro 84%, geothermal 4%); components do not reconcile. Actual 2024: hydro 53.5%, geothermal 19.9%, gas 9.3%, wind 8.9%, coal 5.1%, solar 1.4%.
T4Q3: Low hydro inflows requiring more thermal generation is the correct explanation. Omits the 2.4% to 5.1% shift.
T4Q4: Invents a day-ahead auction and a 'Retailer Supply Auction System (RSA)'. NZ prices in half-hourly real time. Also cites 'Billy', a plan-comparison tool, as a source.
T4Q5: Invents 'Infratil's Genesis Renewables', lists Tiwai Point (a smelter, i.e. a consumer) as a generator, and omits Mercury.
T4Q6: SOE and high-voltage transmission correct. Omits the System Operator role and the 11,000km network - half the expected answer.
T4Q7: Lines companies as regional distribution monopolies is correct. Omits the 29 / 150,000km / 62 retailers figures.
T4Q8: Regulator, rule-setting, competition and reliable supply at least cost all correct.
T4Q9: States demand is expected to decrease and invents '3-4 GWh per household'. MBIE's EDGS (in the KB) projects 62.1 TWh by 2050, +56.6%.
T4Q10: Wind and solar correct. Omits geothermal, gas peaking for firming, and the 96-98% by 2050 projection.
T4Q11: Invents 'production issues at major refineries and import terminals' and gas importing. Omits $800/MWh and industrial curtailment.
T4Q12: Lake Onslow placed 'near Masterton', called a battery facility, 'announced in 2014 but cancelled by the Electricity Authority in 2017'. Every specific is wrong.
T4Q13: Claims Lake Onslow 'was decommissioned in 2019'. It was never built.
T4Q14: Confuses Electrify NZ with Electrify the Hutt - the project's own sponsor. No mention of Fast-Track, RMA changes or NPS reform.
T4Q15: Invents an offshore wind farm '5km off the coast of Otago'. None operate; the Offshore Renewable Energy Act 2026 is the actual answer.
T4Q16: Correct that consenting costs rose. Invents a 'concession boom' quote, attributes to Rewiring, and omits the 70% / $1.29bn Te Waihanga findings.
T5Q1: Net zero by 2050 is right, but the split-gas structure - the substance of the question - is missing, and it cites a non-existent 'Emissions Reduction Plan Amendment Act 2022'.
T5Q2: '47% from 2005 levels by 2050'. Wrong baseline (2017), wrong figure (10% by 2030; 14-24% by 2050), wrong framing.
T5Q3: 50% below 2005 by 2030 correct. Omits the 41% budget-basis equivalent and the 571 Mt budget.
T5Q4: States there is no target beyond 2030. The second NDC (51-55% below 2005 by 2035) was announced 30 January 2025.
T5Q5: Denies an Emissions Reduction Plan exists, substituting EECA's Sector Decarbonisation Programme.
T5Q6: ETS mechanism fabricated: regional allowance allocation, revenue returned to taxpayers, coverage limited to cement and steel. No mention of NZUs or the agriculture exclusion.
T5Q7: 'About 80%' in 2020 against MBIE's 56%, attributed to the Electricity Authority.
T5Q8: Invents an Electricity Authority 'Coal Phase-out Plan' on an 'LCU basis from 1 July 2025'. The actual answer is the reverse: NES-GHG repealed and the 2037 phase-out removed.
T5Q9: Expands GIDI as 'Government Initiative for Decentralised Electrification' funding community projects for low-income households. It is Government Investment in Decarbonising Industry, for industrial process heat.
T5Q10: Invents a Waikato project electrifying 70 homes and 20 jobs, under a third wrong expansion of GIDI.
T5Q11: Name, mandate and advisory role correct.
T5Q12: Names the right agencies but substitutes appliance efficiency standards for the network investment and pricing settings the question is about.
T5Q13: Reaches the right conclusion - no single overarching strategy - and hedges appropriately, but supports it with a fabricated 'Climate Change Response Bill 2022' and an EA long-term plan.
T5Q14: Recasts Fast-Track Approvals as a 2020 Electricity Authority regime for connecting EV chargers. It is a one-stop-shop consenting process for significant infrastructure.
T5Q15: Directionally right that electrification cuts emissions, but the renewable-grid mechanism is absent and the '10% of the national inventory' figure is unverifiable.
T6Q1: PV effect, silicon, freed electrons and current all correct. Omits DC and the 18-22% conversion range; opens with a stray QR fragment.
T6Q2: Mono and poly described correctly in relative terms. No efficiency figures, and thin-film called 'thicker' when it is thinner.
T6Q3: DC to AC conversion and grid synchronisation correct.
T6Q4: Per-panel microinverters vs a shared string, and the shading advantage, both correct. Thin but accurate.
T6Q5: Grid draw, export credit and off-grid battery independence all correct. Omits the larger array requirement and EECA's cost-effectiveness note.
T6Q6: Hybrid = grid-connected plus battery, worthwhile for high night-time use. Omits the outage-backup case. Uses bullets, which the system prompt forbids.
T6Q7: States households 'typically do not sell their excess electricity directly back to the power company'. They can, and EECA says so. Then digresses into outage safety and battery economics.
T6Q8: Usage-from-bills and future needs correct. Omits roof orientation, tilt, shading and daytime occupancy - most of EECA's list.
T6Q9: Solar geometry garbled ('the sun moves from south to north between December and March'), never states that north-facing is optimal, and attributes to NIWA SolarView.
T7Q1: The refrigeration cycle is described incorrectly - the expansion valve is said to raise temperature, the evaporator to give heat to the air, and the water to be heated by the 'cold side'. Closes with a fabricated direct quote attributed to EECA.
T7Q2: Integrated vs split, including retrofit capability, correct.
T7Q3: States the whole cylinder must be replaced. The expected answer is that a split unit can be retrofitted - which Joulie itself said one question earlier.
T7Q4: Invents a 'single-source (single-pipe)' category and an '80% more heat' claim. Both configurations have similar efficiency.
T8Q1: Moves rather than generates heat, extracted from outside air. Final sentence about a 'secondary coil' is garbled but not load-bearing.
T8Q2: COP defined correctly, with the COP-3 worked example.
T8Q3: '3-4 times' against an expected 3-5 times - within tolerance.
T8Q4: Single-split, multi-split and ducted all correctly distinguished, including the ductwork cost caveat. Uses bullets and bold, which the system prompt forbids.
T8Q5: Claims a heat pump 'works just as efficiently at lower outside temperatures'. Efficiency falls as temperature drops, and the defrost cycle - the substance of the question - is never mentioned.
T8Q6: Yes, one unit does both. Omits the reversing refrigerant cycle and calls them 'multi-functional' rather than reverse-cycle.
T9Q1: Electromagnetic field inducing current in the pan, heated by its own resistance, is correct. Omits the coil beneath the glass, the cool surface, and eddy currents by name.
T9Q2: Explains why magnetic cookware is needed but never makes the contrast the question asks for - that gas and radiant elements heat any pan.
T9Q3: Cast iron, carbon steel and stainless correct. Omits enamelled cast iron and magnetic-base nonstick, does not flag that not all stainless is magnetic, and never says what will not work.
T9Q4: Says to check for ferrous material but never gives the fridge-magnet test or the coil symbol - the practical answer.
T10Q1: 'Lithium-ion' is not wrong but skips the LFP-vs-NMC distinction the question is about.
T10Q2: Day charge, night discharge through an inverter, correct.
T10Q3: Reverses the distinction: claims DC-coupled systems 'are only charged by their batteries and may not be able to draw from the grid'. The real difference is where DC-to-AC conversion happens.
T10Q4: Hybrid inverter as a combined grid-tie inverter and battery charger is correct. Trailing QR reference to the 'Your meter' tool is irrelevant.
T10Q5: Answers about V2G instead of the question, and concludes it is 'not yet available'. A home battery can be charged from the grid - yes was the answer.
T11Q1: Gives two options; EECA describes three. The portable 3-pin cable is omitted.

T11Q4: Never explains AC vs DC. Answers on cost and points at an approved-products list instead.

T11Q7: V2G defined correctly, described as emerging in NZ with trials underway, and appropriately hedged.
